module: UDP server that lets you control the game with the BeamNG "remote controller" mobile app. getQRCode opens UDP port 4444 and returns a 5-digit code that the app must send; then each recognized device becomes a virtual device (core_input_virtualInput, type bngremotectrlv1, 1 axis, 2 buttons) fed by the orientation packets received. The vehicle's UI data is sent back to the app (port 4445) via the vehicle's outgauge extension.
notes: Protocol: a packet starting with 'beamng' with three fields separated by '|' (beamng|deviceName|code) is a discovery packet; if the code matches, the game replies 'beamng|code' on port 4445. Other 16-byte packets (struct ori_t w,x,y,z as floats, network order) are read as data: x > 0.5 = button 0, y > 0.5 = button 1, z = axis 0; x,y,z are clamped to [0,1].
A device with no packet for 10 s is removed.
Requires FFI: onExtensionLoaded returns false without it.
BUG: M.onFirstUpdate = onFirstUpdate references an undefined local variable, so this field is nil (harmless).
Packets are read in bursts (loop until receivefrom returns nothing anymore) in onUpdate, every frame (a TODO suggests switching to 1 Hz).
The random code is drawn once when the module loads (random(10000, 99999)).

onFirstUpdate.desc: Is nil: reference to a variable not defined in the file.

getQRCode.desc: Opens the listening UDP socket (port 4444) if it is not open, and returns the pairing code to display (as a QR code by the UI).

returns.desc: 5-digit code, or false if the socket could not be opened.

onUpdate.desc: Update hook: removes devices inactive for more than 10 s, reads UDP packets, creates the virtual devices and emits their events (buttons, axis) to core_input_virtualInput. Does nothing as long as the socket is not open.

returns.desc: false if FFI is unavailable (load refused).

onInputBindingsChanged.desc: Hook called when input bindings change: remembers which player each virtual device is assigned to (key 'vinput<instance>'), or forgets it if the player is negative.

devicesConnected.desc: Indicates whether at least one remote device is connected.

returns.desc: true if there is at least one virtual device.
